 Judgment

The present appellant - Reliance General Insurance Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as "the Insurance Company" for brevity) was respondent No.2, in M.V.C.No.1189/2017, in the Court of the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Hassan (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for brevity), which was instituted by the present respondent No.1, who, as a claimant had instituted a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the M.V.Act" for brevity), seeking compensation of a sum of `18,00,000/- for the injuries alleged to have been sustained by him in a road traffic accident said to have occurred on the date 31-12-2016.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The respondent No.2 herein who was the respondent No.1 before the Tribunal is said to be the owner of the alleged offending auto rickshaw bearing Registration No.KA-46/6716.
2.

The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 31-12-2016,
while he was proceeding as a passenger in auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-46/6716 on B.M.Road, National Highway 75 in Honnavalli at Palya Hobli, Alur Taluk. Due to the rash and negligent driving of the auto rickshaw by its driver, he lost control of the vehicle and the auto rickshaw got toppled, due to which road traffic accident, he sustained injuries.

The claimant has also contended that due to the injuries suffered by him, he has spent huge amount of `4,50,000/-
towards medical expenses and also has suffered with physical disability.

With this, he claimed a compensation of `18,00,000/- from the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 before the Tribunal arraigning The Branch Manager vs Dhananjaya M.S on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71083058/
2 them as the owner and insurer of the alleged auto rickshaw, respectively.

sentences.text: In response to the summons, though both the respondents appeared through counsel, however, it is only respondent No.2 - Insurance Company which filed its statement of objections.
In its statement of objections, respondent No.2 took a substantial contention that at the time of the occurrence of the accident the driver of the auto rickshaw did not possess valid driving licence.
He also denied the alleged medical expenses said to have incurred by the claimant and its liability to pay the compensation.

3. After framing the issues and recording the evidence led by both side, the Tribunal, by its impugned judgment dated 20-09-2019 allowed the claim petition in part, holding the respondent No.2 (appellant herein) before it, liable to pay the compensation to the claimant of a sum of `11,27,120/- together with interest thereupon at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation of the amount.
Challenging the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the appellant - Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.
4. The respondent No.1 herein (claimant) is represented by his counsel.
The second respondent - (owner), though served has remained unrepresented.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant (insurance company) is present through video conference and learned counsel for the respondent No.1 (claimant) is physically appearing before the Court.
6.

Though this appeal is posted for Admission, learned counsels from both side submitted that the matter since is of the year 2020, the same may be taken up for its final disposal, as they are prepared to address their arguments.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that, he has the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits, as such, summoning of the Trial Court records is also not required and that he would place those certified copies before the Court.

With this, the junior counsel for the appellant, who is physically present, places the certified copies of the pleadings,
depositions and exhibits for a perusal and their return to him.
8. In the light of the above, heard the arguments from both side.

Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits placed before the Court by the junior counsel for the appellant.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant -Insurance Company, who has appeared through video conference, in the course of his arguments submits that he fairly concedes that in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663, he would not agitate on the point that the driver of the auto rickshaw not possessing a valid and effective driving licence to drive a passenger vehicle, i.e., auto rickshaw.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN vs. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He submits that he would not address any other grounds raised in the memorandum of appeal except rate of interest ordered by the Tribunal which is at 8%
The Branch Manager vs Dhananjaya M.S on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71083058/
3 p.a. on the award of compensation.

He submits that since the said rate of interest is on the higher side, the same is to be reduced at 6% p.a.
10.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 in her arguments submits that the impugned order does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.
11. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1.

Apart from re-iterating the contents of his claim petition, even in his examination-in-chief also has produced documents from Exs.P-1 to P-30, which inter-alia includes copies of the FIR, complaint, scene of the panchanama,
motor vehicle inspection report, wound certificate, charge sheet, medical bills, OPD bills and case sheets.

Those documents, particularly, from Exs. P-1 to P- 6 would corroborate the evidence of PW-1 about the occurrence of the accident on the date, time and place mentioned by the claimant in the claim petition and also the alleged occurrence and negligent driving of the auto rickshaw by the driver of the said auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-46/6716.
Thus, the occurrence of the road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the auto rickshaw by its driver stands established.
As such, the same does not require detailed re-analysis.

12. In the light of the above, the occurrence of the road traffic accident which is said to have taken place on the date 31-12-2016 involving auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-46/6716 is not in dispute.

Further, it is also not specifically disputed that the present respondent No.1 who was the claimant in the Tribunal was traveling in the auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-46/6716 and in the alleged road traffic accident, he sustained injuries.

13. Before the Tribunal, the present appellant herein - respondent No.2 has taken a specific contention about the alleged absence of a valid and effective driving licence to drive the passenger auto rickshaw by the driver of the auto rickshaw.

After recording the evidence led from both sides,
the Tribunal in its impugned judgment has made an observation at para 15 that in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in MUKUND DEWANGAN (supra) and also in view of the undisputed fact that the driver of the auto rickshaw had a licence to drive LMV, he was not required to obtain a specific licence to drive the offending vehicle and proceeded to hold the insurer also liable to pay compensation.

Since learned counsel for the appellant in his argument submitted that though a ground about the said finding is raised in the memorandum of appeal, he is not pressing the said ground and concedes to observation made in para 15 of the impugned judgment, this Court need not re-visit the said - 10 - aspect again.
The appellant has not even disputed the quantification of the compensation.
In view of the same, the quantification of the compensation also is not being re- visited.
The only ground agitated by the learned counsel for the appellant in the argument is with respect to the rate of interest ordered by the Tribunal.

The Branch Manager vs Dhananjaya M.S on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71083058/
4
The Tribunal has ordered interest at the rate of 8% p.a. on the awarded amount from the date of the filing of the claim petition till the realisation of the amount.

As the alleged date of occurrence of the accident is 31.12.2016 and the date of impugned judgment is 29.02.2019, considering the rate of interest prevailing during the period on the term deposits in the Nationalized Banks, I am of the view that the rate of interest ordered at the rate of 8% p.a. by the Tribunal is slightly on the higher side.
As such, it is only for reducing the rate of interest from 8% to 6%, the present appeal deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed.
The rate of interest ordered at 8% p.a. in the impugned judgment and award stands modified and fixed at 6% p.a.

Rest of the terms of the impugned judgment and award, including quantum of compensation, duration of the payment and interest, the liability to deposit the awarded amount together with interest thereon and its apportionment and release stand unaltered and without any modification.
Draw modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal without delay.
The amount in deposit in this appeal, if any, by the appellant, be transferred to the concerned Tribunal.

Sd/-
